claim_1.claim: Hemagglutination Inhibition analysis of plasma from 212 vaccinated subjects across the 2007–2011 influenza seasons showed antibody responses decreased with age, with the strongest HAI responses in the 2010 season and no significant difference by gender, diabetic status, or race.

sources.quote: In the 2010 and 2011 seasons, in which elderly subjects were included, antibody responses showed a significant decrease with age (Figures 1B, 1C, and S1C), consistent with previous studies (Seidman et al., 2012). Vaccines from different seasons induced varying levels of HAI responses, and there was a significant decrease in the response with age (Figure 1C). Subjects vaccinated during the 2010 season, the year after the H1N1 2009 pandemic, generated the strongest HAI responses. There was no significant difference in antibody response based on gender (Figure S1D), diabetic status (Figure S1E), or race (data not shown).

groups.cohort: vaccinated subjects across the 2007–2011 influenza seasons

claim_2.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMCs from vaccinated subjects across multiple influenza seasons showed that interferon- and dendritic-cell-related BTMs were enriched on days 1 and 3 after primary vaccination (day 1 and day 3), while ASC and cell-cycle-related modules were robustly enriched on day 7 after primary vaccination (day 7) in association with stronger day 28 HAI responses.

sources.quote: BTMs related to the induction of interferons as well as the activation of dendritic cells (Figures 2A and 2B) were enriched on days 1 and 3 after TIV vaccination, whereas modules related to T cells at these time points were negatively associated with the antibody response.
On day 7, there was a robust enrichment of ASC and cell cycle-related modules, consistent with our original study (Nakaya et al., 2011).

claim_3.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMCs from young and elderly vaccinees showed that module-level features predicted HAI responses in both groups, with accuracies of 79.0%–80.2% in young subjects and 64.7%–72.3% in elderly subjects using day 3 and day 7 signatures.

sources.quote: With this approach, we identified BTMs that predicted HAI responses in both the young and elderly groups with accuracies ranging between 79.0% and 80.2% and between 64.7% and 72.3%, respectively, using both day 3 and day 7 signatures (Figure 2C).

comparison.finding: At day 3, module-level BTM features predicted HAI responses in both groups, with higher accuracy in young subjects (79.0%–80.2%) than in elderly subjects (64.7%–72.3%).
At day 7, module-level BTM features predicted HAI responses in both groups, with higher accuracy in young subjects (79.0%–80.2%) than in elderly subjects (64.7%–72.3%).

claim_4.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of baseline PBMCs from combined influenza-season cohorts showed that pre-vaccination B-cell- and T-cell-related modules were positively correlated with increased antibody responses at day 28 after primary vaccination (day 28), whereas monocyte-related modules were negatively correlated with antibody responses.

sources.quote: This approach revealed several B-cell- and T-cell-related modules whose expression pre-vaccination was positively correlated with an increased antibody response to vaccination in all studies (Figure 3A). In contrast, modules related to monocytes were negatively correlated with antibody responses (Figures 3B–3G).

claim_5.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMCs from young and elderly subjects in the 2010 cohort showed the largest age-related difference in vaccine-induced gene expression on day 1 after primary vaccination (day 1), with young subjects exhibiting many more up- and downregulated genes and higher interferon-related gene expression than elderly subjects.

sources.quote: By far the largest difference in overall expression between the two groups occurred on day 1, where the young exhibited a much greater number of both up- and downregulated genes.

Although the genes shared by clusters from young and elderly vaccinated individuals had similar temporal expression profiles, the magnitude of the expression of interferon-related genes differed, being higher in young individuals (Figure 4C).

comparison.finding: On day 1 after primary vaccination, young subjects exhibited a much greater number of both up- and downregulated genes than elderly subjects.
On day 1 after primary vaccination, interferon-related gene expression was higher in young subjects than in elderly subjects.

claim_6.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMCs from young and elderly vaccinees showed that NK-cell-related modules increased with age on days 3 and 7 after primary vaccination (day 3 and day 7), several monocyte modules increased with age on day 7 (day 7), and many B-cell modules decreased in older subjects on both days 3 and 7 compared to younger subjects.

sources.quote: Natural killer (NK) cell-related modules showed increased expression with age on both day 3 and day 7 after vaccination, and several monocyte modules showed increased expression with age on day 7. In contrast, many B cell modules showed decreased expression in older subjects on both day 3 and day 7.

comparison.finding: at day 3, NK-cell-related modules showed increased expression with age and many B-cell modules showed decreased expression in older subjects compared to younger subjects

at day 7, NK-cell-related modules and several monocyte modules showed increased expression with age, while many B-cell modules showed decreased expression in older subjects compared to younger subjects

claim_7.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 cohort subjects showed elderly individuals had higher total NK-cell proportions than young subjects at baseline and all studied time points from days 0–14, with vaccination increasing NK-cell percentages in the elderly but reducing them on day 1 after primary vaccination (day 1) in the young.

sources.quote: Our analysis showed that proportions of total NK cells in elderly subjects were higher than those of young subjects at baseline as well as at all the time points studied (days 0–14). Of note, vaccination induced an increase in the percentage of NK cells in the elderly subjects; in contrast, in the young there was a reduction in the percentage of NK cells on day 1 after vaccination (Figure 5A).

comparison.finding: elderly subjects had higher total NK-cell proportions than young subjects at baseline

elderly subjects had higher total NK-cell proportions than young subjects at day 1; vaccination increased NK-cell percentages in the elderly but reduced them in the young on day 1 after primary vaccination
elderly subjects had higher total NK-cell proportions than young subjects at day 14

claim_8.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMCs from young and elderly subjects showed the elderly had a higher frequency of CD56dimCD16++ NK cells and a lower frequency of CD56++ NK cells at baseline, with CD56dimCD16++ cells increasing in the elderly on day 1 after primary vaccination (day 1), CD56++ cells increasing in the young on day 7 (day 7), and stronger CD69 activation across all three NK subsets in the elderly peaking on day 3 (day 3).

sources.quote: We observed a higher frequency of CD56dimCD16++ cells coincident with a lower frequency of CD56++ cells in the elderly at baseline, consistent with previous studies (Figure 5C; Solana et al., 2014). The distribution of these subpopulations was relatively stable during the response, with CD56dimCD16++ cells showing a small but significant increase in the elderly on day 1 after vaccination and CD56++ cells increasing in the young on day 7.

Elderly subjects showed increasing activation after vaccination in all three subsets, with highest expression on day 3. In contrast, the young exhibited activation of the CD56dimCD16++ subset as measured by CD69 expression only on day 1 and at a lower level than in the elderly.

comparison.finding: at baseline, elderly subjects had a higher frequency of CD56dimCD16++ NK cells and a lower frequency of CD56++ NK cells than young subjects
on day 1, elderly subjects showed a small but significant increase in CD56dimCD16++ cells and higher CD69 activation of the CD56dimCD16++ subset than young subjects
on day 3, elderly subjects showed stronger CD69 activation across all three NK subsets, peaking at day 3, than young subjects
on day 7, CD56++ cells increased in young subjects

claim_9.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMCs from young and elderly subjects showed monocyte proportions were higher in the elderly at baseline and throughout the study, total monocytes increased on day 1 after primary vaccination (day 1) in both groups, and elderly subjects had increased CCR5 but lower CD86 expression in classical and intermediate monocytes compared to young subjects.

sources.quote: In addition to NK cells, we also observed higher proportions of monocytes among the elderly at baseline and during the entire duration of the study compared to young subjects (Figure S6A). In both groups, the percentage of total monocytes in PBMCs increased substantially on day 1 after vaccination, then returned to or below baseline levels.

In both the young and elderly, CCR5 expression peaked in classical and intermediate monocytes on day 1 after vaccination, corresponding with the inflammation associated with the innate immune response. Elderly subjects showed increased CCR5 expression in classical and intermediate monocytes compared to the young, whereas young subjects had higher CD86 expression in these subsets.

comparison.finding: elderly subjects had higher monocyte proportions than young subjects at baseline

elderly subjects had higher monocyte proportions than young subjects at day 1; elderly subjects also showed increased CCR5 but lower CD86 expression in classical and intermediate monocytes compared to young subjects

claim_10.claim: Hemagglutination Inhibition analysis of plasma from a subset of subjects measured through 180 days after primary vaccination showed antibody responses peaked at day 28 (day 28) and declined significantly by day 180 (day 180), with only just over half of day 28 high responders remaining responders at day 180.

sources.quote: The antibody responses peaked at day 28 (D28), with a significant decline in most subjects by D180 (Figure 6A). By applying the same criteria for seroconversion used for the D28 high- versus low-responder classification to the D180 antibody responses, we saw that just over half of D28 high responders maintained their responder status on day 180 (“persistent” responders), whereas the remainder no longer met the criteria for seroconversion on day 180 (“temporary” responders).

comparison.finding: antibody responses peaked at day 28 and declined significantly by day 180; only just over half of day 28 high responders remained responders at day 180

claim_11.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMCs from subjects evaluated for antibody persistence showed plasmablast module BTM S3 was positively associated with day 180 antibody response because of its association with day 28 response, but it was not associated with the day 180/day 28 residual persistence measure; instead, modules related to cell movement and adhesion on days 3 and 7 after primary vaccination (day 3 and day 7) were enriched in subjects with more persistent responses, while day 7 T-cell-related modules were negatively associated with persistence.

sources.quote: As expected, correlation analysis of plasmablast module BTM S3 shows a positive association with the D180 antibody response due to the effect of D28 antibody responses, generated through plasmablast expansion (Figure 6C). However, when we performed correlation between the plasmablast module activity and the D180/D28 residual, we no longer saw an association with the plasmablast expression (Figure 6D).
Among the BTMs most enriched in subjects with a persistent response on both days 3 and 7 were several modules associated with cell movement and adhesion, such as BTM 51 (Figure 6E).

In addition, the day 7 expression of a number of T-cell-related modules was negatively associated with the D180/D28 residual, indicating that increased T cell responses might potentially result in more transient antibody responses (Figure 6F).

comparison.finding: Modules related to cell movement and adhesion were enriched in subjects with more persistent antibody responses at both day 3 and day 7; at day 7, T-cell-related modules were negatively associated with persistence, while plasmablast module BTM S3 was not associated with the day 180/day 28 residual persistence measure.

claim_12.claim: miRNA profiling analysis of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 cohort subjects showed significant differences between young and elderly vaccinees on days 1, 3, and 7 after primary vaccination (day 1, day 3, and day 7), with most differentially expressed miRNAs in the elderly upregulated after vaccination, whereas the young showed predominantly miRNA downregulation.

sources.quote: To assess whether or not miRNAs contribute to the differences in response we saw between young and elderly vaccinees, we measured the miRNA expression profiles of 672 human miRNAs on days 1, 3, and 7 after vaccination from a subset of subjects in the 2010 cohort (Figure 7A). We saw a significant difference in the miRNA profiles between these two groups. Whereas a majority of the differentially expressed miRNA in the elderly were upregulated after vaccination, particularly on days 1 and 7, the young exhibited predominantly downregulation of miRNA.

comparison.finding: significant differences in miRNA profiles between young and elderly vaccinees at day 1; most differentially expressed miRNAs in the elderly were upregulated after vaccination, whereas the young showed predominantly miRNA downregulation
significant differences in miRNA profiles between young and elderly vaccinees at day 3; the young showed predominantly miRNA downregulation

significant differences in miRNA profiles between young and elderly vaccinees at day 7; most differentially expressed miRNAs in the elderly were upregulated after vaccination, whereas the young showed predominantly miRNA downregulation

claim_13.claim: miRNA profiling analysis of PBMCs from young and elderly vaccinees showed miRNA expression correlated with day 28 antibody response, with the elderly having a larger number of miRNAs negatively correlating with antibody response than the young.

sources.quote: We also identified miRNA whose expression correlated with the day 28 antibody response (Figure 7B). We again saw differences between the young and elderly subjects, with the elderly having a larger number of miRNA negatively correlating with the antibody response when compared with the young.

comparison.finding: the elderly had a larger number of miRNAs negatively correlating with day 28 antibody response than the young

claim_14.claim: miRNA profiling analysis integrated with transcription profiling by array in PBMCs showed coordinated miRNA-BTM correlations on day 1 after primary vaccination (day 1), and identified miR-424 as a potential regulator of the antiviral interferon module M75 through predicted targeting of OAS3 and CXCL10.

sources.quote: We then performed correlation analysis between all miRNA-BTM pairs, revealing groups of modules that appear to be regulated together by several miRNA (Figure 7D) on day 1 after vaccination.

Of particular interest was the regulation of module M75-antiviral interferon signature (Figure 7E) on day 1 after vaccination, because the interferon pathway plays a key role during the innate immune response. This miRNA-mRNA network suggests potential novel regulators of the interferon response after vaccination, such as miR-424. This miRNA was predicted to target OAS3, a 2′–5′-oligoadenylate synthase involved in viral RNA degradation (Samuel, 2001), as well as CXCL10, an important chemokine induced by IFN-γ that serves as a chemoattractant for lymphocytes (Dufour et al., 2002).
